caveats: Enrichment results are method-dependent; a ranked test and an over-representation test on the same data can disagree — present these fgsea results as hypotheses for follow-up, not proven mechanism

steps.context: Needs pathway gene sets for the organism: the MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 curated gene sets, HGNC symbols) as the primary collection, and the Reactome human pathway gene sets (HGNC symbols) as the secondary collection, both available as GMT-style reference data for Homo sapiens. Ranking input is the full DESeq2 results table from T1S2 (gene symbol, Wald statistic, for every tested gene).
steps.question: Which biological pathways or hallmark processes are coordinately shifted between treated and control kidney samples, using the full ranked gene list from the DESeq2 batch-adjusted test?
constraints: Rank the full tested gene list — do not pre-filter to significant genes before running fgsea
Report BH-adjusted p-values within each collection separately, not pooled across Hallmark and Reactome
Report the leading-edge genes for every significant set, not just the set names
acceptance_criteria: Every gene tested in T1S2 (not just the significant ones) is ranked by its DESeq2 Wald statistic (the 'stat' column) — this ranking-metric choice is stated explicitly and the unshrunken log2FoldChange or a signed p-value is not used as the rank

fgsea is run against the MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets (primary collection) and the Reactome human pathway gene sets (secondary collection), each restricted to sets with 15-500 member genes among the tested genes; the number of sets surviving this window per collection is reported

Significant gene sets (BH-adjusted padj < 0.05) are reported with NES per collection, and the leading-edge genes are listed for each significant set, with overlap between leading edges of different significant sets flagged as one underlying signal rather than independent findings
The gene-set database and version, the universe (tested genes from T1S2), the ranking metric, and the size window are stated in the output
If either reference gene-set collection cannot be located at run time, the step reports which collection was skipped and completes with whichever collection is available, rather than failing outright

steps.name: Conditional GO Biological Process over-representation
caveats: A hypergeometric test on a short, threshold-sensitive gene list gives an unstable result that changes with the padj cutoff — this is exactly the situation the 50-gene floor is meant to avoid
GO terms nest heavily; without the rrvgo reduction step a single biological signal appears as many redundant 'significant' terms
steps.context: This step is conditional on the size of the T1S2 significant gene list, which is not yet known at planning time. It exists to add a discrete-list GO view when the DE list is large enough to support a hypergeometric test with power; when it is not, this step still runs but reports the skip decision rather than an unreliable result.
steps.question: If the treated-vs-control DE gene list (padj<0.05, from T1S2) is large enough to support it, which GO Biological Process terms are over-represented among those genes relative to all tested genes?
constraints: Universe must be the tested genes from T1S2, not the full gene annotation or full genome
Do not run the hypergeometric ORA test if fewer than 50 genes are significant at padj<0.05 — report the list size and skip instead
acceptance_criteria: The number of DE genes at padj < 0.05 from T1S2 is checked first and reported

If that count is at least 50, enrichGO (or an equivalent hypergeometric GO BP test) is run with the universe set explicitly to every gene that passed the T1S2 pre-filter (never the whole genome or whole annotation)
If the ORA test runs, the resulting significant GO BP terms are reduced to non-redundant representative terms by rrvgo semantic similarity, with the full term table kept as a supplement

If the DE gene count is below 50, the ORA test is skipped, the exact size of the significant list is stated as the reason, and the fgsea result from T2S1 is named as the primary functional-enrichment evidence for this dataset instead

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch covariate
plan.analytical_narrative: The data context gives 12000 x 12 raw integer gene-level counts (salmon-derived, already gene-summarized) for human kidney samples, 6 treated vs 6 control, with two known processing batches balanced across condition. Because the input is already a gene-level integer count matrix (not per-sample transcript quantification files), the standard tximport transcript-to-gene length-offset step is not applicable here — the counts.csv matrix is used directly as the DESeq2 count input, which is standard practice for a pre-summarized gene-level count table. The core question — which genes differ between treated and control — is answered with a DESeq2 Wald test on the design ~ batch + condition, putting the balanced batch in as a fixed covariate rather than pre-adjusting counts (adjusting counts before the model would break the count model's mean-variance relationship and inflate confidence). Sample-structure QC runs first to confirm the batch is not the dominant axis of variance and to catch any outlier sample before the model is fit. An edgeR quasi-likelihood fit on the same design provides a second, independent DE method; only the DESeq2/edgeR intersection is reported as the high-confidence gene set, consistent with recommended practice at 6-per-group replicate numbers. Downstream, the DESeq2 Wald statistic (chosen over the shrunken LFC or a signed p-value because it scales effect by uncertainty and avoids p-value tie-saturation) ranks the full tested gene list for preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (secondary) gene sets available in the reference collection. A GO Biological Process over-representation step runs conditionally: only if the padj<0.05 gene list reaches at least 50 genes, since a hypergeometric test on a shorter list has no power and is threshold-sensitive; otherwise the ranked fgsea result stands as the sole functional-enrichment evidence and the step states why ORA was skipped.
